title: The Effect of Zn Addition on Bioabsorbable Mg Alloys
content: Magnesium has drawn a lot of interest as a possible material for biodegradable implants throughout the past 10 years. Biodegradable implants are preferred over non-biodegradable metallic alloys including titanium (Ti), cobalt-chromium (Co-Cr), and stainless steel because of concerns about secondary infections, metal ion release, and stress shielding. Furthermore, further procedures are frequently necessary for the removal or replacement of conventional metallic implants following patient recovery due to their lengthy healing period and non-biodegradable nature [1].
